dedupe_keys.name: an urbanization monitoring data set for world heritage sites in the belt and road region

description: Xiao and colleagues publish an urbanization intensity index for 79 world cultural heritage sites in the Belt and Road region. The index combines Global Human Settlement Layer, WorldPop population grids and DMSP/OLS night lights to describe development around the sites. Science Data Bank presents the release as PUBLIC and CC0 with one file of 369.66 KB. Its summary reports a mean index change from 0.26 in 2000 to 0.29 in 2015. A modeller could use the site values as context when studying urban growth, heritage access or nearby infrastructure pressure. For simulation, the index could help compare exposure assumptions around heritage sites. The index is a composite of remote-sensing and population inputs, not a record of asset condition, traffic or service capacity. Its site selection is specific to world heritage, so it does not describe every city on the corridor. The repository page does not expose the single file’s format or each site’s time steps in the metadata inspected. No file was downloaded. Related GHSL and population products are inputs; this published site index is a distinct derived resource.
